newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak finmin to participate in c.bank board. [CORRECTED 10:38 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Slovak finmin to participate in c.bank board. [CORRECTED 10:38 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline from "Slovak govt to appoint FinMin to c.bank board" and changes text to make clear that Finance Minister has not been appointed to the central bank governing board but shall be participating in central bank governing board meetings.)
The Slovak government said on Tuesday that Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik will participate in central bank governing board meetings.
The government announced the decision in a short statement saying it had approved a measure charging "a government member with bank board participation".
The statement gave no further details.
Earlier on Tuesday, National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) Spokesman Ivan Paska told Reuters that NBS governor Vladimir Masar had attended the government meeting.
However, he said that Masar had intended to propose its bank supervision department director, Tibor Kasiak, for government approval as a new board member.
Central bank officials were not immediately available for comment. It was not clear whether Kasiak's appointment was discussed at the meeting.

According to the act which sets out the guidelines for the central bank's operation, the government appoints board members and its two chief executive directors based on a proposal by the governor. The act also says the central bank should operate independently from the government.
The president appoints the governor and two vice-governors, based on government proposals and with parliament's approval.
Last week, the government appointed former Deputy Finance Minister Jozef Magula as a board member upon Masar's proposal.
Local bankers have been watching for signs that appointment of new board members by the government could reduce the NBS's independence and lead to any policy changes.
Leading government officials, including Kozlik, have repeatedly criticised the NBS's tight monetary policy.
